item.text: An accessible reading order is the sequence in which assistive technologies—such as screen readers—present a document’s content. It should follow the intended logical flow: headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, captions, and sidebars in a meaningful order. Visual placement alone is insufficient because a document can look correct on screen while its underlying structure orders elements differently. Screen-reader users navigate the structure, not the page layout, so incorrect tagging or object order can make content confusing or misleading.
